steps.label: State variables
lines: describe the equilibrium state of a
steps.margin_note: First mark. Name all four state variables: pressure, volume, temperature and mass.
steps.why: State variables are needed because they are the only quantities that fix the condition of a system; pin down all four and the state is fixed.
common_mistakes: Naming only pressure, volume and temperature. Mass is also a state variable — it fixes the size of the system.
Confusing a state variable with a process such as heating. A process changes state variables; it is not one itself.
steps.memory_tip: Four state variables: pressure, volume, temperature, mass.

steps.margin_note: Second mark. Write the equation of state for an ideal gas, PV = nRT.
steps.why: PV = nRT is the equation of state that joins the four state variables of an ideal gas into a single formula.
common_mistakes: Writing PV = nRT as if it defines pressure or volume alone. It is a relation among all the state variables, not a definition of one.
Leaving out n when the amount of gas is not one mole. PV = RT is the correct one-mole case; PV = nRT is needed otherwise.
steps.memory_tip: PV = nRT is one formula joining all four state variables.

insider_note: Two short definitions. Name all four state variables in the first, and write PV = nRT for the second — nothing more is needed.
